rules.statement: Never register the OpenID provider's server services (`AddIdentityServer`) and the BFF's services (`AddIdentityBff`) in the same service collection; a BFF runs in a host of its own as a client of the provider.
rules.why: A BFF is a client of the OP, so the two never share a process or a service collection. Each process holds none of the other's keys, database or signing credentials.
rules.check: Look for a host or composition method that calls both `AddIdentityServer` and `AddIdentityBff`, or that composes one into the other, on the same `IServiceCollection`.

rules.statement: Don't serve a BFF frontend, or route a path of a frontend's origin, under a path prefix of the authorization server's origin; give each frontend an origin of its own and route every path of that origin to the frontend.
rules.why: A path prefix is not a security boundary. A host-only session cookie with path `/` is sent with every request to its host, so a path routed to another process hands that process the session and shares the origin with its pages.
rules.check: Look for proxy or ingress routes, or endpoint mappings, that put a frontend under a sub-path of the OP's origin, or that forward a path of the frontend's host (for example `/api`) to another process.

rules.statement: Validate a configured upstream service URL at startup with an options validator: it must be an absolute `https` URL with no user info, query or fragment, and `http` is accepted only in the Development environment.
rules.why: The host reads the URL only as configuration and derives nothing itself, so a bad value has to be refused at start instead of failing every call later.
rules.check: Look for a new URL-valued options property that has no startup `IValidateOptions` check, or whose check accepts relative, `http` (outside Development), user-info, query or fragment values.

rules.statement: Don't add a configuration override for a URL that the authorization server accepts in only one form (such as the DPoP `htu` target URL derived from the issuer's origin); derive it instead.
rules.why: The OP compares a DPoP proof's `htu` only with the tenant's published URLs, so an override can only make every DPoP-bound call fail.
rules.check: Look for a new setting or chart value that lets a deployment set the target URL of DPoP-bound calls to something other than the URL derived from the authority's origin.

rules.statement: A host's `Program.cs` holds composition only: it calls the packable library's `Add…`/`Map…` extension methods, and the server's logic lives in that library.
rules.why: The packable library is the composition root, and the host only composes it.
rules.check: Look for options binding, validators, endpoint handlers or other logic written directly in a host's `Program.cs` instead of in the library's composition extensions.
